t: Find Customers With Positive Revenue this Year — Filtering 2021 Revenue
o:
**Understanding the problem**

The Customers table records one revenue figure per (customer_id, year); the composite primary key guarantees at most one row per customer per year, and revenue may be negative. We report every customer whose 2021 revenue is strictly positive. On the sample: customer 1 has 30 in 2021 (kept), customer 2 has -50 (dropped), customer 3 has no 2021 row at all (dropped), customer 4 has 20 (kept) — output ids 1 and 4. Two natural formulations exist: a direct row filter, or a per-customer aggregation that totals the 2021 contribution; the aggregate form keeps working unchanged if the schema ever allowed several rows per customer per year.
k: (customer_id, year) is the primary key, so each customer owns at most one 2021 row and a plain WHERE filter cannot double count.
Positive is strict (> 0), and customers without any 2021 row must be excluded, not treated as qualifying zeros.
SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2021 THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) grouped by customer generalizes to multi-row-per-year schemas.

a.i: Because the primary key ensures a single row per (customer_id, year), selecting the rows whose year is 2021 and whose revenue exceeds zero reports each qualifying customer exactly once. No grouping is required.
s: Restrict to rows with year = 2021 AND revenue > 0.
Return the ids in any order.

c.python:
# Database problem — the accepted submission is a single MySQL query:
SELECT customer_id
FROM Customers
WHERE year = 2021
  AND revenue > 0;

a.t: O(R) — one pass over all R rows of the table

a.i: Group the rows by customer and total only the 2021 contributions with a conditional SUM. A customer qualifies when that total is greater than zero; customers lacking 2021 rows contribute 0 and fail the test. This variant is robust to schema changes allowing multiple rows per year.
s: Compute SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2021 THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) per group.
Keep the groups whose sum is > 0 using HAVING.

c.python:
# Database problem — the accepted submission is a single MySQL query:
SELECT customer_id
FROM Customers
GROUP BY customer_id
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN year = 2021 THEN revenue ELSE 0 END) > 0;

a.t: O(R) — a single grouped scan of the table
a.sp: O(D) for the D distinct customer groups

w:
**Wrap-up**

Prefer the direct WHERE filter in an interview — it states the requirement verbatim and benefits from an index on (year, revenue). Pitfalls: writing revenue >= 0 (zero is not positive), forgetting customers with no 2021 row when using joins (filtering inside an INNER JOIN derived table is safest), and NULL surprises if you swap CASE for IF around missing rows. Follow-up: report the 2021 revenue next to the id — the aggregate form returns it for free with one more column.
